references.text: The same law and the same regulation shall apply to you and to the foreigner who lives among you - this reiterates the principle of one law for both natives and foreigners.
One law shall apply to the native Israelite and to the foreigner who lives among you, when anyone sins unintentionally.
It concerns that the foreigner living among the Israelites must celebrate Passover according to the same regulation and law as the natives.
You shall have one rule; it shall apply to the foreigner just as to the native - affirming equality before the law.
The foreigner who lives among you shall be like a native among you, and you shall love him as yourself.
Here there is no Jew or Greek - in Christ there is no distinction between peoples, which fulfills the principle of one law for all.
The Gentiles who were foreigners to the covenants are now brought near by the blood of Christ and made fellow citizens with the saints.
There is no difference between Jew and Greek, for all have the same Lord - Paul applies the principle of equality for all.
The general law in Numbers confirms and expands the specific principle of equality introduced at the Passover festival.
The eternal nature of equal standing under the law is clarified and elaborated in this regulation.
The principle of one law is extended to also cover the moral and ritual prohibitions against abominable acts.
The principle that foreigners should be treated as natives is expanded from the legal community to apply to the inheritance and property rights of the land.
The principle of one law for foreigners and natives is here specified in relation to sacrificial legislation.
